answer.rationale:
The two observed deteriorations this quarter are mechanical funnel metrics: onboarding completion (-4%) and activation (-6%). Inherited memory points at the same lever twice from independent sessions (memory_31 on cutting signup fields, memory_86 on shortening onboarding), and memory_91 shows activation messaging as a compatible follow-on. Simplifying onboarding attacks the observed regression directly, is cheap to reverse, and does not mortgage unit economics.

I deliberately do not match the competitor's entry pricing, even though memory_73 is the most quantitatively attractive record in the archive (+31% signups, +18% revenue). That is exactly why I want it verified. Its stated lift is a signup-and-revenue lift, not a retained-value lift, and 12 reporting weeks is short enough that discount-acquired cohorts may not have reached renewal. Against a competitor already bidding for price-sensitive SMBs, a 40% discount most likely buys the most churn-prone, lowest-willingness-to-pay accounts, depresses realized ARPU, anchors expectations at the discounted price, and risks cannibalizing existing full-price SMBs who ask to be re-papered. That is a plausible negative against the primary objective of sustainable long-term qualified revenue, so the headline number should not be treated as decision-grade until the source record is read.

I verify memory_73 to test whether its revenue figure is gross bookings or retained/net revenue and whether renewal behavior was observed at all, and memory_86 because it is the record I intend to act on and its "self-serve accounts" scope may not cover the segment where completion is actually falling. If memory_73 turns out to measure durable retained revenue with intact renewals, promotional pricing becomes a genuine contender and I will revisit. If memory_86's population does not match the regressing segment, I fall back to activation_messaging per memory_91.

I am not verifying memory_44 or memory_57: enterprise sales-assist does not address an SMB-side funnel regression on a one-week slot, and referral incentives amplify an acquisition channel that presupposes healthy activation, which is precisely what is currently broken. Running a standard experiment rather than a broad rollout because the causal story behind both declines is still unconfirmed; the declines could be seasonal or traffic-mix effects rather than onboarding friction, and a broad rollout would leave me unable to distinguish the two.
